clue.text: Secure contract

definitions.meaning: to secure something is to get hold of it, as with a fastening or a prize
to contract an illness is to come down with it

explanation.definitionFit: To catch is both to grab and fasten something and to pick up an infection.

clue.text: Entrance to international match inclusive of tax

parts.note: a cap is awarded to a player in an international match, so the player is a cap

indicators.note: inclusive of means the game word holds the tax inside it

parts.note: a tie is a cup match
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Admission to an international game includes a tax charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun about admission; it is the verb, to enchant. A cap is earned by playing for one's country.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or charm them completely.

clue.text: Bloomer by workers' mouthpiece

parts.note: TU is a trade union, a body of workers
lip is impudent talk, and a lip is part of the mouth

explanation.surface: A gaffe made by a union's spokesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip is a spring flower, so it blooms: a bloomer.

clue.text: Family treasures appear vague in sound broadcasts

indicators.note: in sound says the next piece is taken for how it is spoken

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
looms means appears dimly or indistinctly

explanation.surface: Precious heirlooms show up as hazy items in radio programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasts' looks like the noun, but it is the verb, as in to air a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirlooms are valued possessions passed down through the generations of a family.

clue.text: Gluttony, perhaps, when lady dines out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone overindulges at table whenever a certain lady goes out to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals rearranging LADY DINES into DEADLY SIN; 'perhaps' marks gluttony as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is one of the seven cardinal vices of Christian teaching.

clue.text: One called up to a platform in the river

indicators.note: in means the platform sits inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a raft is a floating platform

explanation.surface: Someone is summoned to a floating stage on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river of Wales, England and Scotland. 'called up' means conscripted, not phoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is a conscript, one called up for military service.

clue.text: .Develop sea legs — like Peter Pan, say

indicators.note: develop means work up into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Learning balance at sea, like the boy in the play who sails with pirates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Develop' rearranges SEA LEGS; Peter Pan is the boy who never grows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan never grows older, so he is timeless, never aging.

clue.text: Was quick to put up poor wretch

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a poor devil is an unfortunate person

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to offer lodging to an unlucky soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' in the old sense means alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick once meant alive, so to be quick was to be alive.

clue.text: Place in sun Scipio contrived — that's the suggestion

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A Roman general set in the sun stirs a vague hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges SUN SCIPIO; 'Place in' is surface padding leading into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspicion can be a mere trace or hint, as in a suspicion of garlic.

clue.text: Spacemen left, concerned with air intake

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency

explanation.surface: Astronauts set off, worried about their oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air intake' points to breathing through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, the organ we breathe through.

clue.text: Have a flutter with relish, holding back inside information

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: palate means taste or relish for something

indicators.note: back means the word for inside information is read in reverse

parts.note: a tip is a piece of inside information, as in racing

explanation.surface: A gambler bets eagerly while keeping a racing tip to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a flutter' suggests betting, but here it means the heart racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Palpitations are rapid flutters of the heart, so to palpitate is to beat quickly.

clue.text: Passes for half a dozen soldiers

parts.note: six, written as the Roman numeral VI
the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment

explanation.surface: Six soldiers are issued travel permits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: entry permits.
explanation.definitionFit: Visas are official permits allowing entry to a country, a kind of pass.

clue.text: Drive around motorway to exercise beginner

indicators.note: around signals turning the motorway's name end to end

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written here as MI
PE is physical education, school exercise
L is the learner plate on a beginner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver is taken round the motorway to practise.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to push or force forward, a synonym of drive.

clue.text: Organised team drill — a monotonous routine

indicators.note: organised here means arranged into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports team's drill practice becomes dull repetition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' rearranges TEAM DRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively any wearisome, repetitive round of work.

clue.text: Sailor gets sole or other sea food.

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
sole means single or alone

explanation.surface: A seaman orders sole or some other fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the fish, but it means alone; the abalone is the 'other' seafood beside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible shellfish, a mollusc eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Copying setting for ring with attractive result

indicators.note: setting for means the first word is the mount that holds the other

parts.note: aping means mimicking or copying
a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A jeweller copies a ring's setting to pleasing effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is the sound of bells, not jewellery, and 'setting' is a jeweller's mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Appealing means attractive or pleasing.

clue.text: Novel Moroccan law officer

definitions.meaning: a sherif or shereef is a Moroccan prince; this is a novel spelling of that title
a county's chief officer of the law, in Britain or the US

explanation.walkthrough: SHERIF is a title of the Sultan of Morocco; 'Novel' says the spelling here is an unusual one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff enforces the law in a county; the same spelling is a rare form of the Moroccan princely title.

clue.text: Monarch invades, cuts out manoeuvres

indicators.note: invades means the monarch goes inside the other word

parts.note: excises means removes by cutting
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A king or queen invades and slices bits away during war games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' is the noun, military war games, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercises are military training operations, synonymous with manoeuvres.

clue.text: A ferret that is trained as a circus performer, possibly.

indicators.note: trained means taught new ways, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ie is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A ferret has been taught to be a big-top act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges A FERRET plus IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-eater is a performer who appears to swallow flames, as seen at circuses.

clue.text: Shown, as films may be

definitions.meaning: photographic film is subjected to light when a picture is taken

explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means revealed to view, and film is exposed to light in a camera.

clue.text: Harsh noise from dance centre over the way?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece stands above the second

parts.note: a disco is a dance venue
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A racket from a nightclub across the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' looks like 'middle of dance', but 'dance centre' is a place: DISCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord is a jarring or unpleasant combination of sounds.

clue.text: He picks up fag-end, getting thinner

indicators.note: the end of the word fag is its final letter

parts.note: leaner means thinner, with less fat

explanation.surface: A man stoops for a cigarette butt while growing ever skinnier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fag' is British slang for a cigarette, so 'fag-end' reads as a butt, but it is the last letter of 'fag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner collects leftover grain after the harvest, someone who gathers bits up.

clue.text: Gallery set on closure gets unexpected gift

indicators.note: set on in a down clue means the gallery word sits above the next piece

parts.note: the gods is the highest theatre gallery
an end is a conclusion or closure

explanation.surface: An art gallery closing down receives a surprise donation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the gods' is the top balcony of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is a welcome stroke of luck, like an unlooked-for present.

clue.text: Expert around court is acclaimed

indicators.note: around means the word for acclaimed surrounds the other piece

parts.note: praised means acclaimed or applauded

explanation.surface: A skilled lawyer is widely applauded around the courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert' is an adjective here, skilled, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Practised describes someone skilled through long experience.

clue.text: Sound fruit, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word for fruit as it is heard

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit

explanation.surface: Healthy fruit, or so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective, healthy, but is the verb: to measure depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to measure the depth of water, which is to sound it.

clue.text: Note about fringe subject

indicators.note: about means the note goes around the other piece

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a hem is the edge or fringe of cloth

explanation.surface: A memo on the subject of the edge of a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi...).
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: The point in an action to break off

indicators.note: in means the point goes inside the word for an action

parts.note: a case is a legal action in court
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A litigant finds the moment in a lawsuit to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside CASE; 'point' is a compass direction, not a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to stop or halt, a synonym of breaking off.

clue.text: Fish from the corner

definitions.meaning: to fish with rod and line
a corner is where two lines meet

explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with a rod, and an angle is the meeting point of two lines.

clue.text: Join in fun — it exhilarates

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the next words

explanation.surface: Come and take part in the fun, which is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters running across FUN IT EXHILARATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring together or combine, as joining does.

clue.text: A slip-up in supervision

definitions.meaning: an error or omission made through not noticing

explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is both a careless mistake and the job of supervising.

clue.text: Arrogant soldier returned and took command after start of battle

indicators.note: the start of battle is its opening letter
returned means the word for soldier is turned back to front

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
headed means led or took command

explanation.surface: A conceited soldier came back and led once the fighting began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the reversed soldier after the opening letter of battle; GI is an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigheaded is an informal word for conceited or self-important.

clue.text: Guide animal

explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to direct, and a steer is a bullock raised for beef.
